findings.title: Pairing and the unmatched remainder
findings.claim: In the oath, shaf carries pairing as adding a like to the single, while watr carries the unpaired remainder; pair and odd therefore disclose relational operations alongside their numerical categories.
findings.mechanism: The focus words supply registered pair and single facets. The supplied wide-context account at 89:8 presents Iram through a denial of likeness, giving the pair/unpaired polarity a concrete test: counterparting can fail and leave an unmatched remainder.
findings.reader_payoff: The oath can be felt as a relation between finding a counterpart and remaining without one, while its ordinary even/odd sense stays in view.
findings.containment: The numerical oath reading remains primary. The 89:8 likeness cue and its unresolved م ث ل citation are retained as qualified contextual evidence; this does not assert that 89:3 lexically names Iram or the unresolved branch.

findings.containment: The numerical pair and odd senses remain present. The property branch is retained through its core and specialization facets as attributed HFT evidence; the finding does not accuse every acquisition or supply unregistered context glosses.

findings.mechanism: The focus pair and single facets meet the supplied self, return, reciprocal-satisfaction, and entry occurrences at 89:27-29. The sequence moves from individual identity through mutual acceptance to inclusion, preserving the single while adding relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus polarity no longer requires the single to disappear before it can belong: relation can be added to an intact individual.
findings.containment: The numerical pair/odd reading remains primary. This is a qualified attributed reading of the supplied closing sequence; unresolved context branches remain roles rather than invented lexicon.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace supplies exact focus/context anchors and a changed reading, but its reader identity is legacy-unbound and context morphology is absent.

findings.title: Assembly and tension
findings.claim: The focus pair and single can be modeled materially as joined supports held by a single taut line, while the same fastening logic can harden into restraint.
findings.mechanism: The focus joining facet and the registered watr bowstring facet meet the supplied supports, stakes, and binding in 89:7, 89:10, and 89:26. The contact gives pairing and singulation structural force without replacing their ordinary parity sense.
findings.reader_payoff: Pair and single gain a material tension: joined parts acquire form through a single line, and fastening can move from support toward immobilization.
findings.containment: This is a branch-distant structural analogy retained from an exploratory HFT outlier. It is not a lexical replacement for even and odd, and the unresolved context branches receive no invented glosses.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace provides exact focus/context anchors and a coherent changed reading, but the source explicitly marks the model exploratory, its reader identity is legacy-unbound, and context morphology is absent.
